_note: Business-model rewrite of design/marketing/Architect Landing.dc.html at /for-architects. The design replaced the escrow payout-math card (client funds escrow → 10% platform fee → you keep) with a three-tier subscription section: architects are hired and paid directly and keep 100% of their rate, and the platform's only revenue is their flat monthly plan. The tier rows themselves are already in the DB as payments.SubscriptionPlan (group 'standard': Studio $79 / Practice $299 / Firm $699) — this file supplies the surrounding copy: `plans_label` is the card header ('Choose your plan') and `plans_footnote` the billing line under it. The two keys of the retired payout card, `earnings_example_label` and `earnings_release_label`, are blanked rather than left holding 'On a $14,000 project' / 'Released as you deliver'. `delete` removes the escrow/payout personas that fed that card, plus every stat, step, value prop and FAQ whose natural key the design renamed — seeds/content_copy.json and seeds/content_blocks.json were extracted from the superseded revision and re-seed all of them on every run. Vocabulary throughout: leads → introductions/intros. `tools_link` and `pricing_link` are the entry points to the two dedicated expert pages (design/marketing/Professional Tools.dc.html and Expert Pricing.dc.html): the design ships them as orphans, so this page's tools grid and plan column each link out to the deep dive, the same way the landing page's categories_sub pairs with categories_link.

faqs.question: What does it cost to join?
faqs.answer: Applying is free. Once you’re approved and live, you pay a flat monthly subscription — plans start at $79/mo — and nothing else. We never take a cut of your project fees.

faqs.question: How are leads matched to me?
faqs.answer: The engine matches on your verified license and jurisdiction, your chosen specialties and project types, and your current capacity. You see the pre-scoped introduction and accept or decline — nothing is ever assigned.

faqs.question: How do I get paid?
faqs.answer: You contract and invoice the client directly, at your own rate. Payment happens between you and the owner — we’re not in the transaction and take nothing from it.
